worked_solution:
To find the complex conjugate, we flip the sign of the imaginary part.

In the given number $z=-\sqrt{2}\,i,$ the imaginary part is $-\sqrt{2}\,i$ (there is no real part, just an imaginary part). Flipping the sign, we get $\sqrt{2}\,i.$

Therefore, the complex conjugate is given by $\overset{―}{z}=\sqrt{2}\,i.$
